extraction.input_text: On the issue of whether Albert visited the garage sale, the fact that Tom wrote in an email to Mary that he saw Albert at the garage sale.

claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The statement was made out of court. Tom composed an email to Mary outside of the current proceeding, satisfying the out-of-court requirement for hearsay.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires the statement to be made out of court.
arguments.evidence_span: Tom wrote in an email to Mary

arguments.text: The statement contains an assertion. Tom's email explicitly asserts that he saw Albert at the garage sale, meeting the definition of a statement under FRE 801(a).
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(a) defines a statement as an oral or written assertion.
arguments.evidence_span: that he saw Albert at the garage sale

arguments.text: The statement is offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted. The narrative states it is introduced 'On the issue of whether Albert visited the garage sale,' indicating it is offered for its truth.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) defines hearsay as a statement offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of whether Albert visited the garage sale

arguments.text: The statement is not offered for a non-hearsay purpose. There is no indication the email is offered to show its effect on the listener, for notice, or as a verbal act, reinforcing its hearsay character.
arguments.legal_rule: Statements offered for non-hearsay purposes (e.g., effect on listener, notice) do not constitute hearsay under FRE 801(c).
